findings.issue_text: [High/bug] `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns Zod’s `{ success, data }` result, but it is written directly as `credential.key`, so subsequent Google Calendar reads will not find `access_token` or `refresh_token` at the credential root.

[High/bug] `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177` — with credential sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a Fetch `Response`, but the code treats it as a parsed `HubspotToken`, leaving fields such as `access_token` and `expires_in` undefined.

[High/bug] `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:91` — the sync helper receives `credentialId` as its `userId` argument, sending a credential ID as `calcomUserId` and potentially failing or resolving credentials for the wrong user.

[High/bug] `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:91` — when sync is enabled, the helper returns a Fetch `Response`, but the Axios flow reads `tokenInfo.data`, which is undefined for Fetch responses, so refreshed credentials are not processed.

[High/bug] `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204` — when sync is enabled, the helper returns a Fetch `Response`, while the Axios-based code accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data`, so the refresh path fails to consume the synced token response.

[High/bug] `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75` — Salesforce refreshes directly against Salesforce instead of through `refreshOAuthTokens()`, so credential sync has no effect for Salesforce credentials.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:91` — when sync is enabled, the helper returns a Fetch `Response`, but the Axios flow reads `tokenInfo.data`, which is undefined for Fetch responses, so refreshed credentials are not processed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code wraps the axios call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` (from `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a Fetch `Response` object directly from `fetch()`. However, the code at line 91+ still accesses `tokenInfo.data.error` and `tokenInfo.data.access_token`, which are Axios-specific properties. A Fetch Response doesn't have a `.data` property - it requires `.json()` to be called. This means when credential sync is enabled, the refreshed token data won't be properly processed, causing the credential update to fail silently or error out.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code wraps the axios call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` (from `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a Fetch `Response` object directly from the endpoint. However, the existing code at line 217+ accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate`, which is Axios response structure. A Fetch Response doesn't have a `.data` property - it requires `.json()` to be called. This mismatch means when credential sync is enabled, the code will fail because it tries to access `.data` on a Fetch Response object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75` — Salesforce refreshes directly against Salesforce instead of through `refreshOAuthTokens()`, so credential sync has no effect for Salesforce credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, lines 72-91 show a new fetch call to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' that refreshes tokens directly. The code uses parseRefreshTokenResponse but does NOT wrap the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens() like all other calendar services do (Google, Office365, Lark, Zoho, etc.). This is inconsistent with the pattern established throughout the PR where refreshOAuthTokens() is used to enable credential sync functionality. The finding correctly identifies that Salesforce won't benefit from the credential sync feature because it bypasses the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper.
